- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.  
- If true price drops sharply after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for next 7–14 days if sentiment turns neutral or negative.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a “smooth decay” rule — reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day for days 6–30.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.00 → -0.33 → +0.67), model often misreads momentum; apply a “sentiment momentum filter” — dampen forecast if sentiment swings >0.5 in 3 consecutive days.
